reason: The text portrays elite figures unfavorably throughout. Pharaoh is characterized as stubborn and hardened-hearted (כָּבֵד לֵב פַּרְעֹה), repeatedly refusing to release the enslaved Israelites despite devastating plagues. His resistance to God's commands and his maintenance of oppressive slavery depict him as morally corrupt. The Egyptian magicians (חַרְטֻמִּים) are shown as deceptive practitioners whose power is ultimately revealed as inferior to God's power. Even Pharaoh's servants, while sometimes showing prudent wisdom in recognizing the disasters, remain subordinate enablers of the oppressive regime. The cumulative portrayal presents the Egyptian elite as resistant to divine authority, oppressive in their actions, and ultimately powerless against God's will.
